headline: Labour MPs raise concerns Burnham’s 10-year-plan will not be radical enough

members.title: Labour MPs raise concerns Burnham’s 10-year-plan will not be radical enough
members.lead: Exclusive: Reindustrialisation Research Group to meet with Cabinet Office to discuss worries over PM’s long-term strategy Labour MPs have sounded the alarm over Andy Burnham’s 10-year plan for government, raising concerns that it will not be radical or detailed enough. MPs in the Reindustrialisation Research Group (ReRG), many of whom represent “red wall” seats that helped Labour win the last election, are meeting Sally Jameson, the Cabinet Office minister, on Wednesday to share their concerns about the prime minister’s long-term strategy. members.title: Andy Burnham says government will unveil 10-year plan by mid-December
members.lead: Prime minister tells Kemi Badenoch at PMQs that flagship strategy will be revealed before Commons Christmas recess The government’s flagship 10-year plan will emerge by mid-December, Andy Burnham has told MPs, having previously raised the possibility that it might be delayed until next year. Quizzed by Kemi Badenoch at prime minister’s questions, Burnham told the Conservative leader the plan would be unveiled before the Commons Christmas recess, which begins on 17 December.
